8. Mr Tushar Kanti Roy, learned Advocate appearing for the petitioner by taking me to the plaint, application for rejection of plaint and the orders passed by the Courts below submits that the suit is barred by the principle of res judicata and also barred under section 6A and 102 of the Waqfs Ordinance, 1962 inasmuch as that in view of provisions under section 6A(4) of the Waqfs Ordinance, 1962 the Administrator of Waqfs is empowered to take steps for correction of record-of-rights and the plaintiff, who is a stranger to the waqf estate, has no locus standi to institute the suit and as per the provisions under section 102 of the Ordinance 'Civil Court' has no jurisdiction to decide title in respect of waqf property and accordingly, the plaint should have been rejected by the trial Court. Learned Advocate submits that the revisional Court without considering the relevant provisions of law illegally disallowed the revision by affirming the order of the trial Court and, as such, committed an error of law resulting in an error in the decision occasioning failure of justice and accordingly, interference is called for by this Court. 

 9. As against the above submissions, Mr Faysal Hasan Arif, learned Advocate appearing for opposite party No.1 submits that the question of locus standi as well as res-judicata are mixed questions of law and fact which cannot be decided in disposing of an application under Order VII rule 11 of the Code of Civil Procedure and these issues can only be decided only upon taking evidence during trial. Learned Advocate further submits that admittedly, the suit property is waqf property but the previous mutawalli recorded the waqf property in his name along with his mother in the RS Khatians instead of the name of waqf estate and thereafter, transferred the same without any permission from the Administrator to defendant Nos. 3-7 by way of declaration of heba deed and since the previous mutawalli and his son, the present mutawalli, did not protect the interest of the Waqf, the plaintiff filed the present suit for protection of the waqf property. By referring to the provisions under section 2(8) of the Waqfs Ordinance, learned Advocate submits that 'person interested in a waqf' includes a beneficiary and any person who has a right to worship or to perform any religious rite in a mosque, idgah, imambarah, dargah, maqbara or other religious institution etc, may file a suit to protect the waqf property when the mutawalli goes against the interest of the waqf estate. 

 10. Learned Advocate further submits that though section 6A of 'The Waqfs Ordinance' conferred power upon the Administrator of Waqfs to take immediate steps for correction of record-of-rights which has not recorded in the name of the waqf estate but, in the instant case, the Administrator did not take any steps to correct the record-of-rights. Learned Advocate further submits that in the instant suit not only the record-of-rights has been challenged but also the deed of declaration of heba which has been executed by the previous mutawalli transferring the waqf property to his relatives and mutation khatian have been challenged, the Administrator has no jurisdiction to decide whether the said deed or record-of rights were legal or whether by said deed the defendants have acquired any right, title and interest to the suit land by way of said declaration of heba deed and accordingly, the suit is not barred by law. 

 13. On perusal of the plaint, it appears that the suit has been filed by "ছদাহা লুধী সিকদার পাড়া জামে মসজিদ" represented by the Vice-President of the Committee of the mosque. In the averment of the plaint, the plaintiff stated that 0.40 acre suit land is waqf property out of which 0.30 acre was dedicated by Begumjan and others vide registered deed of waqf dated 17-6-1954 being No. 4345 in favour of the plaintiff mosque and handed over possession thereof in its favour and by said deed Danu Miah was appointed as first mutawalli. Thereafter, Syed Ahmed Mohuri transferred 0.10 acre suit land to the plaintiff vide waqf deed dated 23-11-61 being No.5677 and Md Kamal Hossain, the predecessor of defendant Nos.3-7, was appointed as mutawalli of the waqf estate and in his tenure he recorded said 0.40 acre suit land in his name along with his mother instead of the name of the waqf estate i.e. the plaintiff and thereafter, said mutawalli transferred the suit land in favour of his children (defendant Nos.3-7) by registered declaration of heba deed being No. 1817 dated 4-8-2009. It has also stated in the plaint that the defendants are now claiming title to the waqf property as their personal property and, as such, the waqf estate filed the suit represented by the Vice-president of the mosque Committee praying for a decree of declarations, as stated above. 

 14. As per averments of the plaint, the father of defendant No. 6, who was previous mutawalli recorded the waqf property in his name along with his mother instead of the name of waqf estate and also transferred the suit land by declaration of heba deed dated 4-8-2009 to defendant Nos. 3-7. This averment of the plaint is not denied by defendant No. 6 who is also claiming that he is the present mutawalli of the waqf estate. 

 19. Sub-section (1) of section 6A of the Waqf Ordinance, 1962 provides that 'any immovable property belonging to any waqf estate shall be recorded in the record-of-rights in the name of the waqf and shall be represented by the designation of mutawalli, Receiver or Administrator, as the case may be.' 

 20. Sub-section (4) of section 6A of the Ordinance also provides that 'if any immovable property belonging to any waqf estate is not recorded in accordance with the provisions of this section, the Administrator shall take immediate steps for correction of the record- of-rights. 

 21. In the instant case, admittedly, the record-of-rights of the suit property was not recorded in the name of waqf estate but the same has been recorded in the name of previous mutawalli and his mother. Accordingly, the Administrator of Waqfs should have taken immediate steps for correction of record-of-rights under sub-section (4) of section 6A of the Waqfs Ordinance. By filing supplementary affidavit learned Advocate for the petitioner submits that the Administrator of Waqfs.by order dated 30-3-2015 (Annexure-C-1) directed the petitioner (mutawalli) to take steps for correction of record-of-rights in the name of waqf estate. But, it appears that the petitioner (defendant No. 6) for unknown reasons, did not take any steps in view of the order passed by the Administrator of Waqfs dated 30-3-2015 as yet. 

 23. It appears that the previous mutawalli transferred the waqf property in favour of his children (defendant Nos. 3-6) which has been challenged in the suit. Admittedly, no unction was obtained before the transfer of the suit property by the previous mutawalli. As per section 56(3) of the Ordinance, such transfer shall be declared void, if the Administrator applies to the Civil Court in this behalf. No such action has been taken by the Administrator nor he proceeded against the previous mutawalli under section 32 of the Ordinance. On the other hand, though the Administrator vide order dated 30-3-2015 directed defendant No.6 to take steps to prepare record-of-rights in the name of the waqf estate but he did not comply with the said order and the Administrator did not take any action against

lawyer:
KS Nabi, Advocate -----For the Petitioner. 
Md Serajul Huq, Assistant Attorney-General ----- For Respondent No.1.
parties:
Shawqat Ara Salahuddin and others ----- Petitioner
Vs.
Government of the People’s Republic of Bangladesh and others ----- Respondents
full_judgment:
3. At the first instance, one son, namely, Md Salahuddin preferred this writ petition and obtained Rule on 13-7-92 for a direction to mutate his name in the record of rights as Mr Md Serajuddin, the father of Md Salahuddin died. Later on this Salahuddin died and his heirs have been duly substituted in this writ petition. Subsequently, the other heirs also filed an application for addition of party as petitioners in view of the facts that their names were required to be mutated in the record of rights in place of their predecessor late Md Serajuddin. Now, the position as regards petitioners being heirs of Md Serajuddin stands as follows: 

 5. The petitioners themselves are possessing some portions of the multi-storied building and other portions were let out to different tenants. It is submitted that the petitioners after the death of Md Serajuddin approached respondent No. 1 a number of times in writing and also by appearing before him to mutate the names of the heirs of late Md Serajuddin in terms of the said lease deed dated 26-8-60. On 28-7-87 the heirs of late Mr Serajuddin applied to the Assistant Secretary, Section 7, Ministry of Works, Government of Bangladesh, for mutating their names in terms of the lease deed on the death of Mr Md Serajuddin. The petitioners also gave several reminders for mutation of their names in the record of rights of the Government. On the application of the petitioners the respondent No. 1 by the letter dated 2-8-87 asked the petitioners to submit certain papers and documents as mentioned in the said letter in order to consider their application for mutation. As per letter of respondent No. 1, the petitioners submitted all the documents of title for immediate mutation. Being satisfied with the documents submitted the respondent No. 1 asked the petitioners by letter dated 13-9-87 to deposit a total sum of Taka 77,875.00 being the up-to-date arrear premium of the leasehold property which had fallen due for the said premises. Thereafter, on the direction of respondent No. 1 the petitioners deposited the entire amount of Taka 77,875.00 in TR Form No. 7 with Bangladesh Bank, Dhaka and obtained receipt thereof on 11-1-88. 

 6. In support of their claim for mutation, the petitioners submitted a succession certificate dated 16th May, 1977 which was issued by the District Judge, Dhaka, to respondent No. 1. After verifying the papers and documents in support of the claim for mutation, and finding that the contentions of the petitioners are all true and correct, respondent No. 1 recommended to the relevant authority to record immediate mutation of the petitioners' names and that report is dated 28-1-87. Annexure-1. Thereafter, the petitioners are trying by making representations in writing as well as personally for mutating their names in the record of rights. The relevant authority had given the hope that it would be done soon. But till today this mutation was not completed in favour of the petitioners. Ultimately, the petitioners caused a demand of justice notice dated 5-7-92, but without any result. Under the aforesaid circumstances, the petitioners moved this writ petition and obtained the present Rule. 

 7. It is submitted by the learned Advocate for the petitioners that since the present petitioners are the admitted legal heirs of late Mr Md Serajuddin and since they performed their parts to fulfill the terms and conditions of the lease deed and since the petitioners submitted all the relevant papers and documents required and wanted by the respondents for mutating their names in the record of rights, the respondents are illegally withholding the application of the petitioners for mutation for such a long time. Since there is no lacuna on the part of the petitioners and since all the terms and conditions of the registered deed have been fulfilled and since it is a case of permanent lease for 99 years, the respondents are legally bound to mutate the names of the petitioners as legal heirs of late Mr Md Serajuddin. 

 8. In this case no affidavit-in-opposition has been filed by the respondents. The learned Assistant Attorney-General appearing on behalf of the respondent No. 1 finds it very difficult to oppose this Rule. We have heard the learned Advocate and perused the application as well as the connected annexures and papers. Since there is no denial of the facts stated in the application by the respondents and since the petitioners and their predecessor fulfilled all the terms and conditions of the registered deed of lease and since the petitioners submitted all the relevant papers and documents as required and wanted by the respondents, we hold that the respondents are under legal obligation to mutate the names of the petitioners in the record of rights and this action of illegally withholding the prayer for mutation is absolutely illegal and without jurisdiction. 

 9. In the result, this Rule is made absolute and the action of the respondents in not mutating the names of the petitioners in the record of rights in respect of demised premises of 156 and 157 Motijheel Commercial Area, Dhaka is declared to have been done without lawful authority and is of no legal effect. The respondents are directed to mutate the names of the petitioners in respect of the aforesaid premises of 156 and 157 Motijheel Commercial Area, Dhaka, in place of late Mr Md Serajuddin in the record of rights in the Ministry of Works and in all other relevant records of the Government wherever it is necessary within 60 days from the date of receipt of the copy of this judgment.

lawyer:

Vs.

full_judgment:
2. The short facts of the case are, that the opposite party No. 1 being complainant instituted the aforesaid complaint case in the court of the Upazila Magistrate, Paikgacha, on the allegations that he took lease of the case land from one Amodini Dashi by an amalnama dated 7th Chaitra, 1356 BS and has been possessing the same by paying rents up to date. One Pancharam Saha being plaintiff instituted Title Suit No. 86 of 1985 in the Court of the Assistant Judge, Paikgacha, with respect of the land impleading the complainant opposite party No. 1 as defendant, who has been contesting the same by filing written statement. On 4.5.91 he came to learn from the local Tahsilder that petitioner No.2, the wife of petitioner No.1, recorded her name in pattan Case No. 323 of 1990-91 on the basis of a Kabala No. 688 dated 23.2.91 showing herself as owner with respect to the self-same land and while recording her name in the Revenue Office also submitted another photo copy of a Kabala No. 1742 wherein Amodini Dashi is vendor and accused-petitioner No. 1 is the vendee and thereafter complainant opposite Party No. 1 filed a Review Case under section 150 of the Tenancy Act before the Revenue Officer. Further on the basis of those kabalas she filed an application in the aforesaid title suit for impleading her as a party. 

 6. The learned Advocate for the petitioners next cited the case of Nur Mohammed Vs. Kalimluddin Ahmed, BCR 1987 (AD) 152 wherein their Lordships of the Appellate Division have held that the Objection Officer under the Rules 30 and 31 of the Tenancy Rules 1954 is to decide summarily an objection regarding ownership or possession of land or any interest in land and to record summary of the evidence taken and an abstract of the decision for preparation of records of right. It may be mentioned that Rules 20-24 of the Tenancy Rules deal with the mutation of name in the record of rights, which is exclusively headed by a Revenue Officer. Preparation of record of rights is dealt under Rules 30 and 31 of the Tenancy Rules and the correction of record of rights by way of mutation is also done under Rules 20-24 of the Tenancy Rules before the Revenue Officer concerned and the Revenue Officer dealing with mutation and correction of record of rights is also a Revenue Court. Their Lordships have further held that clause (c) of section 195 of the Code of Criminal Procedure will apply to offences u/s. 467 and 468 of the Penal Code as these are both offences under section 463 of the said Code. 

 8. We respectfully disagree with the above views of the Division Bench which held that Revenue Officer doing mutation matter is not a Revenue Court. Tenancy Rules 30 and 31 deal with preparation of record of rights and Tenancy Rules 20-24 deal with correction of records of rights by way of Mutation. Both the matters are dealt with by the Revenue Officers and regarding Mutation matter there is a provision for review to the Revenue Officer. We are of the view that the principle applicable to preparation of record of right will also be applicable to the mutation of name in the record of rights inasmuch as both relate to preparation, modification, addition or alteration of record of rights. Relying upon the principle as laid down by the Appellate Division in above decision reported in BLR 1987 (AD) 152, we hold that the Revenue Officer dealing in mutation of the name in the record of rights is also a Revenue Court. As we are holding this view relying upon the above decision of the Appellate Division, we need not refer this matter to a Full Bench for our disagreement with another Division Bench.

lawyer:
ABM Nurul Islam with Afifa Begum, Advocates------For the Petitioner.

parties:
Aftab Ali Sheikh (Md) ------ Petitioner
Vs.
Director, Land Records and others ------ Respondents
full_judgment:
Afzal Hossain Ahmed J: This Rule Nisi was issued calling upon the respondents to show cause as to why the order dated 10-7-2001 passed by the Director, Land Records, Directorate of Land Records and Surveys (respondent No.1) and the order dated 1-7-2002 passed by the Zonal Settlement Officer, Jessore Range, Jessore (respondent No.2) should not be declared to have been made and passed illegally and without lawful authority and to be of no legal effect. 

 That 0.54 acres of land of DP Plot No. 3539 of 4532 of DP Khatian No. 975 of Mouza Sannayasgachi, PS Keshobpur District-Jessore belonged to the petitioner's father late Reazuddin Sheikh. During field survey under Rules 28 and 29 of Tenancy Rules, 1955 the aforesaid land was wrongly recorded in the name of respondent No.4 and others against which the petitioner filed appeal under Rule 31 of the Tenancy Rules, 1955 which was registered as Appeal Case Nos. 34806, 34807 and 34808 and were heard and disposed of by judgment dated 21-12-1999 by the Settlement Officer, Jessore allowing the appeals of the petitioner and accordingly, the aforesaid DP Khatian No. 975 was made. Thereafter, on the approach of the respondent No.4, respondent No.1, in excess of the jurisdiction vested in him by law, passed an illegal order on 10-7-2001 directing the respondent No.2 to make correction of the judgment and order passed in the aforesaid appeals whereupon the respondent No.2, Zonal Settlement Officer, Jessore Zone sent the aforesaid appeal cases to respondent No.3, Assistant Settlement Officer, Kaliganj, Jessore for rehearing the decided appeals vide memo No. 17 of 2002 with intent to nullify the judgment made in the appeals under Rule 31 of the Tenancy Rules, 1955. 

 4. Respondent No. 1 has contested the Rule by filing an affidavit-in-opposition contending, inter alia. that the respondent of the said 3 appeals submitted an application to the Director of Land Records to reconsider the judgment and order of the Appellate Officer passed in Appeal Case Nos. 34806, 34807 and 34808 whereupon the Director of Land Records (respondent No. 1) issued letter to the Zonal Settlement Officer, Jessore vide his memo dated 25-7-2000 asking him to submit a detailed report in respect of the case land. Thereafter, upon an inquiry respondent No.4 was found to be in physical possession of the case land. The Zonal Settlement Officer, Jessore accordingly, sent the report to the Director of Land Records on 6-4-2001 whereupon the Director of Land Records (respondent No. 1) directed the Zonal Settlement Officer, Jessore to make necessary correction of the record of rights under Rule 42A of the Tenancy Rules, 1995 vide memo dated 10-7-2001 (Annexure C). Pursuant to this letter the Zonal Settlement Officer vide his memo dated 1-7-2001 (Annexure D) sent the aforesaid 3 appeals to the respondent No.3 for its rehearing. It is further stated that there was nothing wrong in passing the impugned order and that the Director of Land Records is empowered to make such an order dated 10-7-2001 marked Annexure C to make necessary correction in the record of rights, if necessary and that the Rule is devoid of any substance and, as such, it is liable to be discharged with costs. 

 5. Respondent No. 4 has also contested the Rule by filing a separate Affidavit-in-opposition. His contentions are almost similar to those of the respondent No.1 made in his affidavit-in-opposition as above. Besides, he has contended that the Director of Land Records is empowered under Rule 42A of the SA & T Rules, 1955 to review/rehear the appeal heard under Rule 31 of the said Rules. Rule 42A of the said Rules is not a stage of Settlement operation and that the respondent Nos. 1 and 2 can apply it more than once for ensuring justice and preparation of correct record of rights and, as such, the order passed, by the respondent No. 1 dated 10-7-2001 is legal and valid in the eye of law and pursuant to that the order dated 1-7-2002 passed by the Zonal Settlement Officer, Jessore is also tenable, in law and that in the circumstances the Rule is liable to be discharged with costs. 

 6. Mr ABM Nurul Islam, the learned Advocate appearing for the petitioner, submits that the appeal cases being Nos. 34806, 34807 and 34808 of 1999 in respect of the case lands were disposed of on 21-12-1999 vide Annexure A in favour of the petitioner by the Settlement Officer under Rule 31 of the Tenancy Rules, 1955 and thereby creating a new khatian in the name of the petitioner and this shows that the order of the  appellate authority has already been acted upon vide Annexure B. Mr Islam further submits that under Rule 42A of the SA & T Rules, 1955 the Director of Land Records has no legal authority whatsoever to pass an order over a judgment of appellate Court about after 19 months. Under Rule 42A of the said Rules, a Revenue Officer can only direct for correction of the judgment of the appellate Court when an entry in the Record of Rights has been procured by fraud and there is no case that the petitioner procured the appellate judgment by fraud. Thus, the impugned order passed by the Director of Land Records marked Annexure-C, under Rule 42A of the Tenancy Rules, 1955 is totally illegal and without jurisdiction. Mr Islam lastly submits that the Director of Land Records and Surveys is the Executive Head of the entire Land Records and. Surveys Directorate but the Tenancy Act or the Rules has nowhere given him a power to change/amend/correct an appellate judgment and, as such, the impugned order marked Annexure C is not sustainable in law and such an illegal order vitiates everything. 

 7. Ms Syeda Afsar Jahan, the learned Deputy Attorney-General appearing for the respondent No. 1, submits that under Rule 44 of the Tenancy Rules, 1955 the Director of Land Records and Surveys has been vested with the powers to discharge all the functions of a Revenue Officer under Chapter XVII of the SAT Act and shall have all the powers of a Settlement Officer under Rules, 36, 38, 39, 40, 41, 42, 42A and 42B and he, under Rule 42A, may make correction of fraudulent entry before final publications of record of rights. The learned Deputy Attorney-General further submits that since the record of rights has not yet been finally published the respondent No. 1 can make such an order for necessary correction marked Annexure C and there is no illegality in passing the impugned orders. 

 8. Mr Hasan Foez Siddique, assisted by Mr Munshi Mohammad Ali, the learned Advocate appearing for the respondent No.4, submits that it cannot be said that the Director of Land Records and Surveys was totally without jurisdiction in passing the impugned order. Rules 36, 39, 42A and 44 of the Tenancy Rules read with Rules 34, 41, 42 and 46 of the State Acquisition and Tenancy Rules, 1955 and section 150 of the State Acquisition and Tenancy Act clearly provided that the Director of Land Records and Surveys is also a Revenue Officer as well as a Settlement Officer and he has got the administrative control over all the matters under his Directorate. Mr Siddique further submits that it will be seen from the impugned order that the Director of Land Records and Surveys, considering the materials on record, particularly reports of the Charge Officer and Zonal Settlement Officer found some error in the orders of the Settlement Officer in appeals and, as such, he directed to take necessary steps as per provisions of Tenancy Rules. So, it cannot be said that the respondent No.1 was totally without jurisdiction in passing the impugned order and in these circumstances the Rule is liable to be discharged with costs. 

 10. The question to be decided in this case is, whether the Director of Land Records and Surveys was legally authorised to pass an order directing the Settlement Officer to make necessary correction, under Rule 42A of the EBT Rules, of the judgment and orders passed in appeal cases being Nos. 34806, 34807 and 34808 of 1999. 

 11. The petitioner has challenged Annexure C dated 10-7-2001 whereby the Director Land Records and Surveys passed the order under rule 42A of the EBT Rules 1955, directing the Zonal Settlement Officer, Jessore for correction of the judgment and order dated 21-12-1999 passed in the aforesaid Appeal Cases by the Settlement Officer under Rule 31 of the EBT Rules vide Annexure A to the writ petition. Admittedly, the petitioner filed the appeals as above under Rule 31 before the Appellate Officer (Settlement Officer) who having heard both the parties and considered the facts, circumstances and materials placed before him allowed the appeals on 21-12-1999 by creating a khatian in his name and  accordingly, a Khatian marked as Annexure B to the writ petition has been created in his name. It shows that the order of the appellate authority has been acted upon vide Annexure B. 

 "42 A. Correction of fraudulent entry before final publication of record-of-rights- The Revenue-Officer, with the additional designation of 'Settlement Officer' shall, on receipt of an application or on receipt of an official report for the correction of an entry that has been procured by fraud in record-of-rights before the final publication thereof, after consulting relevant records and making such other enquiries as he deems necessary, direct excision of the fraudulent entry and his act in doing so shall not be open to appeal. At the same time, the Revenue-Officer shall make the correct entry after giving the parties concerned a hearing and recording his finding in a formal proceeding for the purpose of future reference." 

 13. From a plain reading of rule 42A, it is apparent that a Revenue Officer can only direct correction of an entry procured by fraud but not the judgment of the appellate Court. In the instant case it appears that there is no case that the petitioner procured the appellate judgment by fraud inasmuch as the appellate judgment, marked Annexure A, was passed after giving a full-fledged hearing to both the parties and on consideration of the relevant papers. Under Rule 44 of the Tenancy Rules 1955, the Director of Land Records and Surveys has been vested with the power to discharge all the functions of a Revenue Officer under the said chapter and shall have all the powers of a Settlement Officer under Rule 42A along with some other Rules in respect of all operations under Chapter XVII of the SAT Act but unless there is a case of fraud or having procured the appellate judgment in making the entry by fraud Rule 42A of the Tenancy Rules, 1955 has no manner of application. 

 14. As the Director of Land Records and Surveys has specifically mentioned in his order that he. passed the order (Annexure C) under Rule 42A of the EBT Rules, there is no scope to argue that the Director of Land Records and Surveys passed the impugne order under any other provision of law. Therefore, the argument advanced by the learned Advocates for the respondents that the order might have been passed under Rule 44 or under any other Rules does not hold good and there is no scope to travel beyond Rule 42A of the said Rules. 

 15. The Director of Land Records and Surveys is the Executive Head of the Directorate of Land Records and Surveys but the Tenancy Act or Rules has nowhere given him power to change/amend correct an appellate judgment and, as such, prima facie, the impugned order dated 10-7-2001 passed by the respondent No.1, marked Annexure C, whereupon the order dated 1-7-2002 marked Annexure D was passed by the respondent No.2 both appear to have been passed without lawful authority. 

 19. The impugned order dated 10-7-2001 passed by the Director, Land Records, Directorate of Land Records and Surveys (respondent No. 1) and the order dated 1-7-2002 passed by the Zonal

No one ----- For the Petitioners. 
Sultan Ahmed Deputy Attorney-General with Malik Sayed Ahmed ----- For the State, OP.

Idrish Ali & Another ----- petitioners
vs
State ----- Respondent
full_judgment:
8. The precise meaning of judicial power was given by Griffith, CJ in the case of Huddart Parker & Co. vs Moorhead, 8 CLR 330 at page 357 where he said: I am of opinion that the words 'judicial power' as used in section 71 of the Constitution mean the power which every sovereign authority must of necessity have to decide controversies between its subjects, or between itself and its subjects, whether the rights relate to life, liberty or property. The exercise of this power does not begin until some tribunal which has power to give a binding and authoritative decision (whether subject to appeal or not) is called upon to take action." This definition was accepted by the Privy Council as the best definition of judicial power in the case of Shell Co. of Australia Ltd. vs Federal Commissioner of Taxation, 1931 AC 276. 

 11. This Court had also the occasion to analyse the different attributes of a Court in several decisions. In the case of IDBP vs M/s. Master Industries (1974) 26 DLR 157 and in the case of Shamsul Huq Sikder vs Election Tribunal & others, (1975) 27 DLR 388 it was laid down that "the exercise of judicial power of the State is the determining factor for investing a body with the character of a Court and that a Tribunal exercising a judicial power does not mean merely that it is acting with fairness and impartiality on a proper consideration of all relevant materials after giving an opportunity to all contending parties to present their respective cases. In order that exercise of judicial power or acting judicially may be a sign of acting as a Court, it must be acting as a part of the judicial machinery of the State, charged with the duty of determining the rights of one subject against another or a question of right between the subject and State and discharging its function according to established form of judicial procedure." 

 13. Mutation proceedings are done under the State Acquisition and Tenancy Act and the Rules framed thereunder. So let us now examine the provisions of the State Acquisition and Tenancy Act and the Rules framed thereunder, insofar as those relate to the powers and duties of a Revenue Officer and the procedure he follows in mutating one's name in the record-of rights. 

 14. Section 143 of the State Acquisition and Tenancy Act provides, inter alia, that the record-of-right prepared or revised shall be maintained up to date in the prescribed manner under Part IV, or under chapter XVII by correcting clerical mistakes and by incorporating the changes on account of (a) the mutation of names as a result of transfer or inheritance. 

 22. Duties of Tahshilder: (1) The Tahshilder or Patwari shall be primarily responsible for reporting promptly to the Revenue Officer immediately superior to him (apparent clerical mistakes in the record-of rights,) all charges in the owner-ship of land, all cases of alluvion, diluvion and reformation of land and the particulars or unsettled lands, in his area................... 

 23. Duties of Revenue Officers :- (1) The Revenue Officer shall, if he is vested with necessary powers in this behalf under the Act, incorporate, and if he is not vested with such powers, send up proposals to the officer vested with such powers for incorporating necessary changes in the record of rights— 

 24. Duties of officers entrusted with the work of maintaining the record-of-rights :- (1) Subject to the provision of sub-rule (2), the officer entrusted with the work of maintaining the record-of-rights shall promptly incorporate therein all changes reported to him under rule 23. 

 (2) Before incorporating any change in the record-of-rights, the officer shall carefully examine the report on the basis of which the change is to be made and shall satisfy himself about its correctness and for that purpose he shall follow such procedure and take such action as may be directed by the Board of Revenue. 

 On an analysis of the rule in the light of the tests indicated above we are unable to characterise the functions assigned to a Revenue Officer as judicial functions. Under the rules a Revenue Officer is invested with the power of mutation of names but he has to act on the report of a Tahshilder. The primary responsibility lies with the Tahshilder to report to the Revenue Officer when any change in the ownership of land takes place. Upon this report the Revenue officer incorporates the necessary change in the record of-rights. It he is not vested with the requisite power in that behalf he sends up a proposal to the officer vested with such power for incorporating the necessary changes in the record-of rights when mutation of names is allowed as a result of inheritance or transfer. Before sending the proposal, the Revenue Officer may, however, make enquiries and take such evidence as he may think fit so as to satisfy himself as to the correctness of the report. The enquiry he makes appears to be an enquiry conducted by an up-to-date record-of-rights. He does not decide anything by a definitive judgment. The decision he gives is subject to the determination of the right by a civil Court. The mere fact that such an officer has been invested with the power to take evidence in course of an enquiry in a mutation proceeding does not make him a Court. His order of mutation is "merely an executive order" as held by a Division Bench of the Dhaka High Court in the case of SM Lutfullah vs Bibi Badrunnessa, (1968) 20 DLR (Dhaka) 1019. In view of the above it is patent that a Revenue Officer holding mutation proceeding does not act as a Court within the meaning of section 195(1)(c) Criminal Procedure Code. 

 17. The view we have taken finds, support from the decision of the Privy Council in the case of Nirman Singh vs Thakurlal Rudra Protap Narain-Singh, AIR "1926 PC 100. In that case their Lordships held that mutation proceedings, is "in the nature of fiscal-inquiry instituted in the interest of the State for the purpose of ascertaining which of the several claimants for the occupation of certain denominations of immoveable property may be put into occupation of it with greater confidence that the revenue for it will be paid" and that it was an error to suppose that such proceedings are "judicial proceedings in which the title to and the proprietary rights in immoveable property are determined."

full_judgment:
Md Akram Hossain Chowdhury J : On an application under Article 102 of the Constitution, this rule nisi was Issued calling upon the respondents to show cause as why the impugned order dated 9-5-2011 passed by the Land Appeal Board (Full Board), in Case No. 2-3/2010 (Full Board) Moulvibazar, dismissing the appeal and maintaining the order dated 24- 6-2003 passed by the Assistant Commissioner (Land), Kulaura in Miscellaneous Case No. 16/ 2002-03, directing the Kanongoo and Upozilla Land Assistant Officer for correction of the record as Khas land in respect of the land of Plot No. 1569 of Khatian No. 366 measuring an area of 32 decimals, Plot No. 1569 of Khatian No. 369 measuring an area of 50 decimals, Plot No. 1049 of Khatian No. 382 measuring an area of 32 decimals, plot No. 1650 of Khatian No. 386 measuring an area of 36 decimals and Plot No. 1652 of Khatian No. 386 measuring an area of 60 decimals, in total 2.07 acres of land under JL No. 65/174, Mouza-Purba Monsurabad, Kulaura, District -Moulvibazar as contained in Annexure-L to the petition should not be declared to have been made without lawful authority and is of no legal effect and as to why the respondent No. 7 should not directed to allow mutation in the name of the petitioner in respect of the aforesaid land and/or why such other or further order or orders as to this Court may deem fit and proper, should not be passed. 

 2. The facts leading to the rule as averred in the writ petition, in brief, are that the petitioner was claiming that their ancestral land measuring 2.07 acres along with other lands were originally belonged to one Boishnav Chandra Deb who died leaving behind two sons namely, (1) Nagendra Chandra Deb and (2) Ganenra Chandra Deb; Ganendra Chandra was unmarried and died leaving behind his only brother Nagendra as his heir; Nagendra Chandra died leaving behind his son Champa Deb i.e. the present petitioner and one daughter Mira Rani as his heirs and thereby the petitioner owned the aforesaid land by way of inheritance. The petitioner used to possess the land in question but the SA Khatian Nos. 382, 386, 366 and 369 containing those property have been prepared in S.A. operation in the name of his father Nagendra Chandra Deb and his grandfather Boishnab Chandra Deb. However, since the petitioner being only son of his father Nagendra Chandra Deb and is possessing the land in question, as such, in the recent survey DP Khatian No. 1083 has been prepared in his name. After the death of his father, Nagendra Chandra Deb who was the SA recorded tenant, the petitioner filed Mutation Case being No.1730/2001-02 before the 'respondent No. 7, the Assistant Commissioner (Land), Kulaura for mutating his name in separate khatian but in the meantime one Md. Mahmud Ali, the respondent No. 9 herein, with a view to grab the petitioner's ancestral property filed another Mutation Case being No 1327/2001-02 before the aforesaid respondent No. 7 under section 143 of the State Acquisition and Tenancy Act, 1950 (shortly SAT Act). Then both the mutation case were heard together by the respondent No.7, the Assistant Commissioner (Land), Kulaura who after hearing by his order dated 10-11-2002 (Annexure-C) rejecting: both the mutation case directed the Tahsilder, respondent No. 8 to sent a proposal for declaring the land in question as government Khas land. In pursuant to that order of respondent No. 7 dated 10-11-2002 a Miscellaneous Case being No. 16/2002-03 was started for declaring the land in question as government khas land; in which behind the back of the petitioner, the respondent No. 9 collusively managed to have obtain a report dated 21-11-2003 stating that there is no heirs of the SA recorded owner Nagendra Chandra Deb in Bangladesh and thereby the respondent No. 7 vide his order dated 24-6-2003 (Annexure-D (1) directed the Kanongoo and Upazilla Land Assistant Officer (ULAO) to correct the khatian of record to the 90 Champa Deb vs Bangladesh (Md Akram Hossain Chowdhury .1) 21 BLC (2016) effect that the land in question is a government khas land. Thereafter, the petitioner against the order of the respondent No. 7 dated 10-11-2002 passed in Mutation Case No. 1730/2001-02, filed Miscellaneous Appeal No. 5/2004 before the respondent No. 6, the Additional Deputy Commissioner (Rev.), Moulvibazar who after hearing the parties by his order dated 29-6-2004 (Annexure-E) sent the matter/case back on remand to the, respondent No. 7 to re-consider and dispose of the Mutation Case No. 1730/ 2001-02 after examining the documents and the identity placed by the petitioner. As per the remand order of respondent No. 6 dated 29-6- 2004 the respondent No. 7 again started a Miscellaneous Case being No. 2/2004-05 and after hearing vide his order dated 29-5-2005 (Annexure-F) rejecting the Misc. Case. No. 2/2004-05 uphold his earlier order passed on 10-11-2002. The petitioner challenging the said order of the respondent No. 7 dated 29-5-2005 again filed Miscellaneous Appeal No. 3/2005 under section 147 of the SAT Act before the respondent No. 6, Additional Deputy Commissioner (Revenue), Moulvibazar who after hearing the said appeal vide order dated 6-9-2005 (Annexure-G) dismissed the same with an observation that the, petitioner, if so desire, may sought his relief before the competent Civil Court. 

 3. By this time the respondent No. 9, Md. Mahmud Ali also filed Miscellaneous Appeal No. 4/2005 before the respondent No.6 against the order of respondent No. 7 dated 24-6-2003 passed in miscellaneous Case. No. 16/2002-03 in order to correction of the record to the extent of the land in dispute as government khas land. After hearing the said appeal the respondent No. 6 dismissed the same with an observation that the respondent No. 9, Md Mahmud Ali may take legal recourse by filing an application before the Exchange Regularization Upazilla Committee (ERUC) or to file a civil suit in order to have the decision about his title through the alleged exchange deed. Accordingly, the respondent No. 9 though filed an application before the Exchange Regularization Upazilla Committee (ERUC) but no such deed of Exchange bearing No.7560 dated 9-12-1968 was submitted at the time of filing of .the mutation case before the respondent No. 7, as such the petitioner filed a written objection thereon. 

 9. It appears from the record that the present writ petition is a certiorari in nature, as because the legality and validity of the impugned Judgment and order was called in question; as such, the Lower Courts record requires to be examined but no LCR was called for at the time of issuance of the rule. However, the petitioner annexing the judgment and orders of the respective authority concerned obtained the present rule; and after that upon filing supplementary affidavits, other relating documents have also been filed by both the parties; hence, we find that so far as the judgments and other relating documents being filed, by this time, to this writ petition, as such, now it is convenient to this Court, without the Lower Court's record the present rule can be disposed of upon perusing and going through the annexures as annexed by both the party to this writ petition. 

 12. Mr Bishajit Roy, the learned Deputy Attorney General appearing with Mr. Swamp Kanti Deb, learned Assistant Attorney General appearing on behalf of the respondent No. 5 by filing an affidavit-in-opposition contended that the respondent No. 7, the Assistant Commissioner (Land), Kulaura upon complying all the process and formalities as provided under section 92 in as much as 92 (2) of the State Acquisition and Tenancy Act, 1950 initiated the Miscellaneous Case No, 16/2002-03 for treating the property as a government Khas land; because of that the property in question was being found abandoned and admittedly recorded as wasteland (পতিতভূমি) in the SA khatian. The property in dispute was being found ownerless and uncared of and therefore, the respondent No.7 upon hearing the objections of the parties under section 92 of State Acquisition and Tenancy Act declared the property as government khas land. The learned DAG in support of his submission showing some khatians annexed to his affidavit in-opposition as annexure-2 series submits that the disputed property has already been shown in the recent published khatian as khas land and the Miscellaneous Case No. 16/2002-03 has been disposed of by correcting the records having there is no title of any persons other than the government of Bangladesh and showing that the property in question is a government khas land. He further submits that since the SA record was prepared showing the land as wasteland (পতিতভূমি) and abandoned, thereby the respondent No. 7, Assistant Commissioner (Land), Kulaura rightly treated the property as government khas land. The Land Appeal Board being the last Court of facts in deciding the case under section 147 of the State Acquisition and Tenancy Act, 1950 having found the process has been complied with legally and rightly, as such, affirming the order of the respondent No. 7, Assistant Commissioner (Land) Kulaura dismissed the appeal which deserves no interference. 

 It also appears from the record that the present petitioner though filing a mutation case sought for mutating his name in separate khatian by claiming his title by way of Inheritance before the respondent No. 7 but he failed to prove his identity and presence in Bangladesh when the mutation case was taken up for hearing and also failed to prove as to the presence of S.A. recorded owners of the land in question i.e. the predecessors of the petitioner who were all along residing in this country. In appeal the respondent No. 6, Additional Deputy Commissioner (Rev), Moulvibazar initially upon hearing the appeal remanded the case to the Assistant Commissioner (Land) for rehearing the petitioner and also to examine his identity. Pursuant to that order of remand, though the Assistant Commissioner (Land), Kulaura heard the matter elaborately again and examined the documents supplied by the petitioner but found the petitioner's identity is questionable and upon holding an inquiry on the land in question found that the property was shown as wasteland (পতিতভূমি) as well as abandoned and also being uncared of Accordingly, the respondent No. 7 again decided the case holding that the land in question is being found ownerless and thereby upholding his earlier order passed in Miscellaneous Case No. 16/2002-03 declared the property in question as government khas land. In appeal under section 147 while the matter was again taken up for hearing in review, the Additional Deputy Commissioner (Rev.), Moulvibazar found the title as appears from the pleadings of the respective parties are questionable and thereby dismissing the appeal has given a chance to the parties concerned to agitate their grievances before a competent Civil Court in deciding their title on the disputed land. However, the petitioner and respondent No.9 challenged the said decision of the Additional Deputy Commissioner (Rev.), Moulvibazar before the Additional Divisional Commissioner, Sylhet but the Additional Division Commissioner, Sylhet ultimately though passed a conflicting order, eventually at the end of the proceeding the full board of the Land Appeal Board finally uphold the decision of the respondent No. 7, Assistant Commissioner (Land), Kulaura. 

 14. It reveals from the record that in deciding the Miscellaneous Appeal No. 5/2004 the Additional Deputy Commissioner (Rev.), Moulvibazar in its order dated 29-6-2004 observed- 

 143. Maintenance of the record of rights-The Collector shall maintain up-to-date, in the prescribed manner, the record-of-rights prepared or revised under Part IV, (or under this part) by correcting clerical mistakes and by incorporating therein the changes on account of- 

 143B. Correction of the Record-of-Rights upon inheritance-(1) Persons acquiring immovable property by inheritance according to their respective personal laws shall amicably effect partition of the property among them after the death of the propositus. After such partition, an instrument of partition shall be prepared and signed by all the concerned parties and shall be registered under the Registration Act, 1908. 

 143C. Procedure for Correction of the Record-of-Rights-(1) The Revenue officer on receipt of the notice under section 89 shall open a file for mutation of record-of-rights and shall issue notice to the co-sharers of the holding for mutation. 

 (2) For this purpose the Revenue-officer shall fix a date for objection if any. If no objection is raised within the stipulated period, the Revenue-officer shall correct the record-of-rights accordingly. 

 (3) If any objection is filed by any co-sharer of the holding, then the Revenue-officer shall fix a date for hearing both the parties, and after hearing, the Revenue-officer shall pass an order stating the reasons thereof, and the record-of-rights shall be corrected accordingly. 

 (3) Before entering on a holding under sub-section (2), the Revenue-officer shall cause a notice to be published in the prescribed manner declaring his intention to so enter on the holding and specifying the reasons thereof and also inviting objection from all persons interested in the holding and shall consider any objections that may be submitted to him within the period specified in that behalf in the notice and shall record a decision. 

 16. Upon going through and careful scrutiny of the above such provisions of law and the judgment and order passed by the Revenue Officer as well as the appellate authority under sections 143, 147 and 150 of the State Acquisition and Tenancy Act, 1950 respectively, we find that Most of the authorities under this Act came to' a decision that the title of the suit property is very much questionable and from the SA record and the BS record the property in question appears to have been recorded as a wasteland (পতিতভূমি) As such the title of the disputed land could not be decided in a summary proceeding under sections 143 and 147 of the State Acquisition and Tenancy Act, 1950. However, it also reveals from the record that the procedure under section 92 has been properly compiled with in extinguishing the interest of the original raiyat in treating the property as khas land and the petitioner and respondent No. 9 who claimed their respective title over the land having interest thereon challenged that decision by filing appeal under section 147 of the said Act. 

 17. In view of the above facts and circumstances we find reliance to a decision reported in 41 DLR 364 wherein Mr. Justice Mustafa Kamal, the then Hon'ble Chief Justice of Bangladesh, in deciding the case of Syed Ashfaque Hossain vs Government, of Bangladesh, in his Judgment at poragraph-25, referring to a unreported judgment of the Appellate Division passed in Civil Appeal No. 8 of 1972, the case of Bangladesh vs. Marium Khatun, categorically observed. "Section 143 of the Act is attracted only when a clerical mistake is to be corrected or, inter-alia, the mutation of names as result of transfer or inheritance is necessary. It is not attracted when the record-of-rights is to be corrected after a finding to be-given as to the title of the holders or the challengers. The examination of title deeds for purposes of determinating title of the holder of record of rights is not permitted under section 143.

full_judgment:
2. Facts necessary to dispose this appeal are that the appellants herein as the petitioners (hereinafter referred to as the writ-petitioners) filed the above mentioned writ petition before the High Court Division challenging Memo No. Parti: 21/97/576 dated 28-5-1997 issued by writ-respondent No.2, the Director General, Directorate of Land Record and Survey, Government of the People's Republic of Bangladesh, Tejgaon, Dhaka with a direction upon writ-respondent No.3, the Settlement Officer, Dhaka to correct the order dated 25-4-1996 passed by writ-respondent No.4, the Assistant Settlement Officer, Dhaka Southern Office of the Land Record and Survey, Tejgaon, Dhaka. 

 3. In the writ petition, it was stated, inter alia, that respondent No.5, the Capital Co-operative Housing Society Limited, as the petitioner filed Writ Petition No.1080 of 1989 before the High Court Division impleading the Director, the Settlement Office and the Assistant Settlement Officer, all of Land Records and Survey, Tejgaon, Dhaka, appellant No.1 herein (hereinafter referred to as writ-petitioner No.1) and 18 others challenging the order dated 5-2-1989 passed in Appeal Case Nos. 34046 of 1984 to 34054 of 1984 heard analogously by way of review by the Assistant Settlement Officer to have been passed without lawful authority and was no legal effect and to declare the striking out the name of the writ-petitioner (the Capital Co-operative Housing Society) from the RS Khatian No.1600(DP) as illegal and without any basis and lawful authority and also to declare the inclusion of the names of respondent Nos. 3-21 (in Writ Petition No.1080 of 1989) in the RS Khatian as fraudulent and without any basis. Subsequently, by filing a supplementary affidavit a prayer was added as to why the order dated 18-1-1989 passed by writ-respondent No.1 (a), the Settlement Officer be not declared to have been passed with-out lawful authority and was of no legal effect. 

 4. The case of the writ-respondent No.5 (in the instant writ petition) in Writ Petition No.1080 of 1989 was that the land recorded in CS Khatian Nos. 138 and 330 bearing Plot Nos.881, 890, 893, 894 with a total area of 9.46 acres land and plot Nos.878, 879 with an area of 2.86 acres land respectively within Mouza-Uttar Khan, formerly within Police Station-Keraniganj, now Police Station-Gulshan, Dhaka originally belonged to Sharafatullah who died leaving behind 4(four) sons named Abdur Rahman, Pokai, Nazimuddin, Faizuddin and one daughter named Jewar Bibi. Bhawal Raj Estate, superior landlord of the case land, got a rent decree against the said tenants for arrear of rents in respect of CS Khatian No.330 and put the decree into execution and auction purchased the lands of this khatian and got delivery of possession thereof on 20-2-1930 and the said landlord also got another decree in a title suit against the said tenants and filed an execution case for the realization of the decretal costs, attached and put the lands of CS Khatian No. 138 in Court sale, auction purchased the same and got delivery of possession thereof on 20-6-1940. Subsequently, the said landlord settled the lands of those two CS Khatians with one Rahmat Banu on 3-3-1943 and she also got her name recorded in the SA Khatian and as she was threatened to be dispossessed from the case lands, she filed Title Suit No.80 of 1965 in the 1st Court of Munsif, Dhaka for permanent injunction against the successors-in-interest of said Sharafatullah and the purchasers, but as eventually, she was dispossessed from the case land, she filed another suit being Title Suit No.9 of 1970 in the 5th Court of Subordinate Judge, Dhaka for declaration of title and for recovery of possession which was decreed in her favour and she got delivery of possession of the case land and later on, the said writ-petitioner purchased the entire lands from Rahmat Banu by a registered sale deed bearing No.10884 dated 24-3-1978 and got delivery of possession thereof. 

 7. On 2-4-1995, one Suruj Mea and his 28 co-sharers, on 19-4-1995, one Motiur Rahman and his two co-sharers, on 21-4-1995, one Majir uddin and another co-sharer and on 23-4-1995, Manwara Begum separately submitted four applications before respondent No.2 who directed respondent No.3 for taking legal steps upon examining those applications and in compliance with the said direction, Syed Ahammad Gazi, Assistant Settlement Officer was assigned to enquire into the matter and he submitted an enquiry report on 8-5-1995. Considering the said enquiry report, comment of the Assistant Settlement Officer and recommendation of the charge officer, it was found that there were some mistakes and irregularities in the matter of apportioning land in the draft records of rights prepared earlier, the Settlement Officer, respondent No.3 vide his order dated 17-9-1995 started Miscellaneous Case No.3439 of 1995 under rule 82A of the State Acquisition and Tenancy Rules, 1955, in short, the Rules, 1955 in order to remove the mistakes and irregularities and to prepare correct record of right and directed Joynal Abedin Bhuiyan, Assistant Settlement Officer to submit his opinion to the Settlement Officer for approval, after hearing the matter upon giving notices on the parties. 

 8. Writ-petitioner No.2, purchased-"in-possession" from the successive heirs-in-interest of said Sharafatullah and their vendee was added as opposite party in Miscellaneous Case No.3439 of 1995 vide the order dated 8-10-1995. After receipt of the notices, all the parties concerned recorded in the said RS Khatian No. 1600(DP) and also respondent No.5 appeared in the said miscellaneous case and contested the same. After perusing the said four applications, order dated 5-2-1989 passed in the said nine appeals, the judgment passed in Writ Petition No.1080 of 1989 and hearing the parties, Joynal Abedin Bhuiyan, the Assistant Settlement Officer, vide his order dated 2-1-1996 passed in Miscellaneous Case No.439 of 1995 proposed to prepare the RS Khatian in the names of the successive heirs-in-interest of said Sharafatullah and the petitioners along with other purchasers in possession from them after deleting the names of said Rahmat Banu and Capital Co-operative Housing Society Ltd (writ-respondent No.5 in the instant writ petition) from draft RS Khatian No.1600 and on 4-1-1996 submitted his said proposal before respondent No.3 for approval. Respondent No.3 after consulting the records vide his order dated 5-4-1996 accepted/approved the said proposal of Joynal Abedin Bhuiyan and ordered preparation of the record of right in conformity with the approved proposal and directed him to carry out the said order. Joynal Abedin Bhuiyan, vide his order dated 25-4-1996 carried out the earlier order dated 5-4-1996 passed by respondent No.3 and prepared the final RS Khatian No. 1600 of Mouza-Uttarkhan, Police Station-Gulshan Dhaka in the name of the petitioners and other successive heirs-in-interest and the purchasers-in-possession from them under rule 32 of the Rules, 1955. Thereafter the said RS Khatian No. 1600 was published finally under Rule 33 of the Rules, 1955 and a certificate stating the fact of such final publication was made by the revenue officer under rule 34(1) thereof. And then in the official Gazette Notification dated 26-9-1996, a declaration under rule 34(2) of the Tenancy Rules, 1955 was made by the Government to the effect that the records of right of Mouza-Uttar Khan, Police Station-Gulshan, Dhaka was finally published under section 144(7) of the State Acquisition and Tenancy Act, 1950. Following the said Gazette Notification dated 26-9-1996, respondent No.1 vide Memo No. Bhu:Ma/Sha-3/ Bhu:U :Ka/20/94/234(123) dated 6-10-1996 directed all concerned persons including respondent No.2 to take necessary steps so that fixation of LD Taxes and other functioning in this regard were done on the basis of the said finally published RS Khatians and thereby RS Khatian No.1600 was acted upon. Respondent No.5 having failed in Writ Petition No.1080 of 1989, tried to mislead and influence various authorities including the offices of respondent Nos. 1 and 2 with an intention to get extra procedural, extra statutorily and extra-judicial benefits and privileges and in course of his said improper attempts, respondent No. 2 vide his office Memo No. Prati:/21/97/576 dated 28-5-1997 passed order directing correction of the record of rights stating that an illegal order dated 25-4-1996 was passed for preparation of record of rights, when the matter was finally settled in appeal and preparation of record of rights was in the last stage of printing. The impugned Memo dated 28-5-1997 was issued without giving the writ-petitioners any chance to be heard, though the same was entirely prejudicial for them. Writ-petitioner No.2 and one Mosammat Mallika Begum being unofficially informed of the impugned order dated 28-5-1997 on 16-6-1997 submitted a memorandum to the State Minister for Land to cancel the same and the State Minister forwarded the said memorandum to writ-respondent No.2 with a direction to consult the matter with writ-petitioner No.2 who though met writ-respondent No.2, went in vain. There-after, writ-petitioner No.2 and said Mosammat Mallika Begum on 5-10-1997 submitted another memorandum to the State Minister of Land with the same prayer which was forwarded to writ-respondent No.1 vide Memo Bhu:Ma/Sha-2 (Prakalapo/17/97-503 dated 21-10-1997 with a direction for enquiry by the Director (Record), Land Record and Survey Directorate, but the said Memorandum has still been kept in abeyance. On 26-4-1998 the concerned officers visited the case land for further preparation of the record of rights thereof and they verbally informed the writ-petitioners that they were officially bound by the impugned order dated 28-5-1997 to prepare the said record of rights in accordance with the same. 

 12. Respondent Nos.6-11 got themselves added in the writ petition by filing separate petitions. Added respondent No.6, Syed Golam Mostafa filed an affidavit-in-opposition to contest the Rule contending, inter alia, that the case land belonged to Bhawal Courts of Wards. One Sharafatullah took settlement of that land from Bhawal Estate; Bhawal Estate instituted Rent Suit No.2525 of 1927 for arrears of rent; that suit was decreed; thereafter the Bhawal Courts of Wards purchased the suit land in auction in Rent Execution Case No.373 of 1928 on 20-2-1930; Bhawal Court of Wards got possession of the land through Court on 20-2-1930; Bhawal Court of Wards thereafter settled the land with Rahmat Banu on 22-3-1943; legal heirs of Sharafatullah filed Title Suit No.652 of 1930 challenging the aforesaid auction; that the said suit was dismissed on contest on 10-9-1930; that the legal heirs of Sharafatullah filed Title Appeal No.1011 of 1930 on 17-3-1931 which was also dismissed; thereafter the plaintiff of Title Suit No.652 of 1930 filed Second Appeal No.2927 of 1931 before the High Court Division which was also dismissed; thus auction purchase was confirmed by all the three Courts; that one Zewar Bibi, daughter of Sharafatullah filed Title Suit No.113 of 1946 for declaration of title; that the suit was dismissed on 6-1-1948; Zewar Bibi filed another suit being Title Suit No.31 of 1950 renumbered as Title Suit No.72 of 1951; that suit was dismissed on 19-4-1952; that on 22-12-1964 Zewar Bibi filed title appeal (number is not available from the record) against the aforesaid judgment which was also dismissed; accordingly, the land was recorded in the name of Rahmat Banu who took settlement from the landlord auction purchaser; the heirs of Sharafatullah took barga of the case land from Rahmat Banu; since the Bargadars stopped giving barga paddy to Rahmat Banu, she filed Title Suit No.9 of 1970 against Asia Khatun and others (legal heirs of Sharafatullah); that suit was decreed on 22-8-1972; that Rahmat Banu got possession in Title Execution Case No.6 of 1973. The Bargadars filed First Appeal No.6 of 1976 before the High Court Division; that appeal was dismissed on 30-4-1975 for non prosecution, thus title of Rahmat Banu was again reaffirmed; that on 23-3-1978 Rahmat Banu by a registered sale deed sold the case land to Capital Co-operative Society, i.e. respondent No.5; that respondent No.5 being a developer developed the case lands, divided the same into 155 plots and distributed those to 155 members who constructed pucca and semi pucca residential houses and have been residing in those houses; that in pursuance of the aforesaid registered sale deeds, the respondents and the other allottees got their names duly mutated and paid rents to the Government upto 1996, but because of the dispute as mentioned in earlier paragraphs the Government was not taking any ground rent from the allottees. 

 13. Writ-petitioner No. 1 (appellant No.1) filed a supplementary affidavit stating, inter alia, that the original owner of the land of CS Khatian No.330 of Mouza 195, Uttar Khan under present Police Station-Uttar Khan was one Bholanath Singh and from whom Sharafatullah, son of late Robiullah became the owner and possessor under sthitiban rayoti title in respect of Plot Nos. 878, 879, 881, 890, 89. 994 measuring in total 12.32 acres land and the name of Sharafatullah was correctly recorded in CS Khatian Nos.138 and 330. After the death of CS recorded tenant, Sharafatullah, the name of one Rahmat Banu appeared in SA Khatian Nos. 239 and 434 in respect of the aforesaid 12.32 acres land appertaining to those six plots and, as such, the heirs of Sharafatullah at the time of last RS operation filed 9(nine) objection cases under rule 30 of the Rules, 1955 and those objection cases were allowed in part. Respondent No.5 (Capital Co-operative Housing Society Ltd) being aggrieved by and dissatisfied with the order passed in the aforesaid 9(nine) objection cases filed 9 (nine) appeals under Rule 31 of the Rules, 1955 bearing numbers: 34046-34054 of 1984 and on consideration of the papers and documents those appeals were finally dismissed on contest by the Assistant Settlement Officer, Dhaka Zone, Dhaka by his order dated 5-2-1989 with a direction to record the names of the objector appellants only in RS Khatian No.1600. As it appeared from annexure-' Ka', respondent No.5 settled the properties of SA Khatian Nos.239 and 434 covering 6 plots of original CS Khatian Nos.138 and 330 measuring 12.32 acres land by way of perpetual lease to 162 persons and after they lost in the settlement appeals under rule 31 being Nos.3446-3454 of 1948, filed Writ Petition No. 1080 of 1989 and obtained a Rule Nisi; the Rule Nisi issued in the aforesaid writ petition was discharged on 2-3-1993; Another Division Bench by its judgment and order dated 14-11-1991 in Writ Petition Nos.207 and 208 of 1989 dealing with more or less the same principle of law involved in Writ Petition No.1080 of 1989, amongst others, declared that the Director General of Land Records could not exceed his power by entertaining and disposing of a second review petition against the order passed by the Settlement Officer in appellate jurisdiction in respect of correction of record of rights. Respondent No.5 did not challenge the judgment and order dated 2-3-1993 passed in Writ Petition No.1080 of 1989 before this Division and thus accepted the result of their above mentioned writ petition, but got a series of suits filed through their lessees before the 1st Court of Subordinate Judge, Dhaka impleading the writ-petitioners as defendant Nos.27 and 34 respectively and respondent No.5 as pro-forma defendant No.55. Writ-petitioner No.2 was contesting those suits by filing written statements and to the knowledge of the petitioners, respondent No.5 was giving active support and assistance to the plaintiffs of those ongoing title suits in which they challenged the Gazette being No. ভুঃ মঃ/শাঃ-২(গঃ বিঃ)-৭৪-৯৫-৩৯২ dated 24-9-1996 in respect of RS Khatian No. 1600 more or less attracting the subject matter of the writ petition. 

 "Mr. Rokonuddin Mahmud, learned Counsel, appearing for the petitioners submit-ted that after preparation and final publication and gazette notification of khatian on completion of all legal requirements as provided in State Acquisition and Tenancy Act, 1950 and the State Acquisition Rules, 1955 there was no scope for the respondent No.2 to reopen the issue on any pretext and in these circumstances, the High Court Division seriously erred in law in holding that the impugned memo is merely a communication from one office to another to perform certain official acts and committed gross injustice in discharging the Rule on the ground of maintainability alone without going to the merit of the case; that after publication of the official gazette notification under section 144(7) of the State Acquisition and Tenancy Act, 1950 read with Rule 34(2) of the State Acquisition Rules, 1955, the record of right is to be presumed to be correct under Rule 35 of the said State Acquisition Rules which can only be declared incorrect by the competent memo issued by the respondent No.2 is without jurisdiction and is liable to be declared to have been made without lawful authority and is of no legal effect; that all the necessary parties were made parties in the writ petition and, as such, the case law referred to by the High Court Division are not applicable in the present case. The learned Counsel further submitted that having regard to the provision of rule 42 of the State Acquisition Rules, 1955 which vested the Revenue Officer appointed with additional designation of 'Settlement Officer' with the power to direct cancellation of any portion of the proceedings referred to in rules 28 to 30 in respect of any district or part of a district or local area at any time before publication of the final record of rights, the High Court Division was wrong in failing to hold that the impugned order passed by the respondent No.2 after publication of the gazette notification dated 24-9-1999 under section 144(7) of the State Acquisition and Tenancy Act, which is final, directing the Settlement Officer to correct the record of right in favour of respondent No.5 upon finding that the direction dated 24-4-1996 to publish the record of rights in the name of the petitioner and others, ultra vires, the provision of the said rule 42 and is without lawful authority, arbitrary and malafide." 

 19. From the impugned judgment and order, it appears that the High Court Division discharged the Rule Nisi on the findings, inter alia, that: (i) The interest of the writ-petitioners (there were two writ-petitioners) in the case land was not stated in the writ petition; it was not clear what quantum of land belonged to each of them "singularly and/or jointly" and how they would be aggrieved if the survey records were amended pursuant to the impugned Memo; (ii) the impugned memo did not contain any quantum of land or mention any specific plot number or khatian number except referring to the land "as that recorded in the name of Capital Co-operative Housing Society Limited in Mouza-Uttar Khan"; (iii) the occupants and the owners of the land in question had not been made parties, if the Rule Nisi was made absolute as prayed for by the appellants, then all the persons in possession of the concerned land and the persons who claimed title thereof would be adversely affected. They also had a right to be heard before any order could be passed affecting their interest in the land, no one except certain officials connected with the Land Record and Survey and Capital Co-operative Housing Society Limited represented by its Chairman were made respondents; (iv) the appellants impugned memo No.Prati:21/97/576 dated 28-5-1997 issued under the signature of writ-respondent No.2, Director General, Directorate of Land Record and Survey, Tejgaon, Dhaka addressed to the Settlement Officer. Dhaka regarding correction of records in Mouza-Uttar Khan in the name of Capital Co-operative Housing Society Limited stating that the land survey records prepared as per rules in the name of Capital Co-operative Housing Society Limited was at the last stage for publication; that after hearing the appeal through an illegal order dated 25-4-1996 under rule 42 of the Rules, 1955, an order was passed for recording the said land in the name of some other persons; the Director General, Land Records and Survey, after enquiry found the said order illegal and gave direction for correction of the survey records as per the rules; (v) the impugned Memo was merely a communication from one office to another to perform certain official acts and that was not acted upon. 

 22. The impugned memo was annexed to the writ petition as annexure-'F'. A perusal of the same shows that the same was not communicated to the writ-petitioners and it was a correspondence made by the Director-General of the Land Records and Land Survey, the Government of Bangladesh, Tejgaon to one of its Settlement Officer. In the writ petition, the writ-petitioners also made statements that—"As the writ-petitioners were not served upon any copy of the said memo dated 28-5-1997 they collected an attested copy thereof from the office of the respondent No. 1 and the same is annexed hereto and marked as annexure-'F'." From the above statements, it is clear that the impugned memo was not communicated to the writ-petitioners. Internal correspondence unless communicated to the person concerned cannot be the basis of cause of action for moving the High Court Division under its power of judicial review and we hold that since the copy of the impugned memo was not communicated to the writ-petitioners, no cause of action arose to seek any remedy challenging the said Memo.
